key_insight: APO is an unsupervised alignment method that improves 3D atomic structure prediction by optimizing physically plausible structures without requiring ground-truth coordinates.
engineering_relevance: This could reduce labeling cost and accelerate structure prediction workflows for crystals and proteins in data-scarce scientific and engineering applications.
method: Uses group-relative policy optimization adapted to 3D atomic systems.
Introduces a dual-reward design: a structural-mode reward from eigen-decomposition of sample similarities and a thermodynamic stability reward.
Lets the model self-correct by favoring physically consistent configurations within sampled groups.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports benchmark gains on crystal and antibody structure prediction, with better match rates, structural fidelity, and more efficient inference via straighter probability paths.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well the unsupervised rewards capture true physical validity, so stability criteria and similarity grouping likely need careful tuning.
paper_title: APO: Unsupervised Atomic Policy Optimization for 3D Structure Prediction of Atomic Systems
